script: Three reasons Japanese couples sleep in separate beds. First, it has nothing to do with a failing relationship. It is actually about prioritizing rest. Japanese work hours are notoriously brutal, and accidentally waking up your exhausted partner is considered incredibly rude. Next, temperature preferences are a massive deal. Summers there are intensely humid, so instead of fighting over the air conditioning settings all night, couples simply sleep in different rooms. But the biggest reason? The kids. Japanese mothers traditionally co-sleep with their babies and toddlers for several years. Because standard beds are relatively small, the husband usually gets banished to his own room just so the baby has enough space.
title: The Great Emu War
hook_text: Three reasons Japanese couples sleep in separate beds.
